chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the G risk allele more strongly and activates MYC
chains.element: rs6983267 lies in a candidate 8q24 enhancer element whose activity is allele-dependent.
chains.cell_type: HCT 116 colorectal carcinoma epithelial cell line (DepMap ACH-000971)

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele at rs6983267; TCF7L2 is chosen as the canonical TCF/LEF-family colorectal enhancer factor, but no QBiC-SELEX evidence list was supplied.
The ref G allele increases activity of the candidate 8q24 enhancer element containing rs6983267.
The enhancer element regulates the nearby MYC oncogene, increasing MYC expression when the G allele is present.
The effect occurs in colorectal carcinoma epithelial cells, represented by HCT 116.
G allele-dependent TCF7L2 enhancer activity and higher MYC expression increase colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP or EMSA shows ref G > alt T binding at rs6983267.
A G-versus-T enhancer reporter shows higher activity for G in HCT 116 cells.
MYC expression is higher with the G allele in an allele-sensitive colorectal cell context.
G is the risk-associated allele for colorectal cancer.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 binding is not stronger on the ref G allele than the alt T allele at rs6983267.
The G allele does not increase enhancer activity or MYC expression in HCT 116 cells.
The disease association is fully explained by a linked variant and not by rs6983267.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated allelic effect at rs6983267
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding at rs6983267.
No allele-specific enhancer activity or MYC expression difference attributable to rs6983267.
Any colorectal cancer association is due to a linked causal variant, a passenger event, or no allelic effect.
falsified_if: A reproducible allele-specific TF binding difference and allele-specific enhancer/MYC effect are shown at rs6983267 in colorectal cells.
The disease association at rs6983267 is shown to be independent of linked variants and dependent on this variant's enhancer activity.

chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the T allele more strongly and represses MYC
chains.element: rs6983267 lies in a candidate 8q24 enhancer element whose activity is allele-dependent.
chains.cell_type: HCT 116 colorectal carcinoma epithelial cell line (DepMap ACH-000971)

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the alt T allele more strongly than the ref G allele at rs6983267; this is a competing direction-of-effect model.
The alt T allele increases TCF7L2-bound enhancer activity, but the enhancer acts as a repressive element in this context.
The repressive effect occurs in colorectal carcinoma epithelial cells, represented by HCT 116.
Lower MYC expression associated with the alt T allele reduces colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 binding shows alt T > ref G at rs6983267.
A T-versus-G enhancer reporter is more active for T, but MYC expression is lower with T.
T is protective relative to G for colorectal cancer.
TCF7L2 knockdown reverses the allele-dependent MYC effect.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 binding is not stronger on the alt T allele than the ref G allele at rs6983267.
The T allele does not reduce MYC expression in HCT 116 cells.
The variant effect is not repressive or is not mediated by TCF7L2.

chains.title: A related TCF/LEF factor TCF7L1 mediates the G-allele effect
chains.element: rs6983267 lies in a candidate 8q24 enhancer element whose activity is allele-dependent.
chains.cell_type: HCT 116 colorectal carcinoma epithelial cell line (DepMap ACH-000971)

links.claim: A related TCF/LEF-family factor, TCF7L1, rather than TCF7L2, binds the ref G allele more strongly at rs6983267; this competing family member is not distinguished without QBiC-SELEX, expression, and ChIP evidence.
The G allele increases activity of the candidate 8q24 enhancer element through TCF7L1.
TCF7L1-bound enhancer activity increases MYC expression.
The effect occurs in colorectal carcinoma epithelial cells, represented by HCT 116.
G allele-dependent TCF7L1 activity and higher MYC expression increase colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: Allele-specific ChIP shows TCF7L1 binding is G > T at rs6983267.
TCF7L1 knockdown, but not TCF7L2 knockdown, reduces the allele-dependent enhancer/MYC effect.
The G allele remains risk-associated in colorectal cancer.
falsified_if: TCF7L1 binding is not stronger on the ref G allele at rs6983267.
TCF7L2, rather than TCF7L1, accounts for the allele-specific binding and enhancer effect.
The MYC effect is not TCF7L1-dependent.

matrix.test: Allele-specific TCF7L2 binding assay at rs6983267 in HCT 116: EMSA with ref-G and alt-T probes, or allele-specific ChIP-qPCR if the cells are heterozygous.

outcomes.outcome: ref G binds TCF7L2 more than alt T
alt T binds TCF7L2 more than ref G
ref G binds TCF7L1 more than alt T
no allele-specific TF binding at rs6983267

matrix.test: G-versus-T enhancer luciferase reporter in HCT 116 cells, with and without TCF7L2 knockdown.

outcomes.outcome: G enhancer is more active and increases MYC reporter activity
T enhancer is more active but represses MYC reporter activity

matrix.test: Allele-specific MYC expression measurement after CRISPR base editing or allele-specific enhancer perturbation at the endogenous 8q24 locus in HCT 116.

outcomes.outcome: G allele raises endogenous MYC in a TCF7L1-dependent way

next_experiment: The single cheapest first experiment separating the top two chains, C1 and C4, is an allele-specific TCF7L2 binding assay at rs6983267 in HCT 116: EMSA with ref-G and alt-T probes, or allele-specific ChIP-qPCR if HCT 116 is heterozygous. It tests whether ref G binds TCF7L2 more strongly, as C1 predicts, or whether there is no allelic binding difference, as C4 predicts. It does not by itself test enhancer activity, MYC expression, or a linked causal variant; those require reporter/expression or LD/fine-mapping follow-up.
